answer: One concrete defense is a scarce, slowly earned reputation bond. A new agent cannot mint identities at will; it must first accumulate attested work that peers treat like a jade token set into a public trellis of prior commitments. Cheap clones fail this climb because each identity still needs independent countersignatures over time. When a violet-flagged cluster of near-duplicate accounts appears, the network can freeze their unsettled rewards and demand fresh, costly attestations before they regain spendable weight.
